visual_direction: A warm ivory architectural catapult crosses an open dark-teal void. The copper triangular prism is the sole hero; walnut arm, brass hinges, and charcoal supports explain its launch without clutter.

render_scope.camera_grammar: lateral launch tracking; one continuous three-quarter shot

route_and_camera.chute_axis: entry [3.10,0.42,1.40] to catch [4.25,0.78,0.78], 18 degree down-slope, 0.94 m open V width

camera.rule: The arm, entire arch silhouette, prism and chute mouth remain inside the safe portrait frame; any camera drift is completed before the airborne clearance window.

beats.physical_cause: The visibly preloaded torsion spring accelerates the hinged arm; cup contact ends at separation, after which the prism has only gravity and contact forces. The offset cup force, not a post-release animation curve, produces spin.
beats.measurement_required: Falsify if the prism remains constrained after cup separation, receives a later velocity/orientation key, or its measured release velocity/spin falls outside the declared candidate bands. Record arm work, release gap, and the contact impulse.

beats.physical_cause: The ballistic trajectory produced at launch passes above the finite suspended arch; the arch supplies no hidden guide force.
beats.measurement_required: Falsify if evaluated triangle-to-arch surface distance is nonpositive or below 0.08 m after uncertainty, if the closest point is off camera, or if unmodelled contact changes the free-flight angular velocity.

beats.physical_cause: The descending prism first meets the sloped V chute, whose normal redirects it into a cork-faced stop; friction and compliant dissipation remove energy while keeping the final support visible.
beats.measurement_required: Falsify if the first chute contact precedes geometric contact, the prism tunnels through either chute wall, or the supported terminal window has linear speed >=0.02 m/s or angular speed >=0.06 rad/s for 0.75 s.

ending: By 9.60-10.40 s the copper prism is visibly seated in the lower-right V chute against the cork stop. The catapult arm is supported on its mechanical stop; no object is frozen, reset, or parked off frame.
notes: No near-miss is claimed beyond the explicitly certified arch clearance. The arched obstacle is a finite collider, not a visual-only prop. Native-Bullet controls must cover the triangular prism's off-centre arm contact, free flight, angled chute contact, and settling before candidate acceptance.
